result:
Done. The premise turned out to be false, and measuring first is what saved this from a bad change.

## What I measured

The entire repository history packs to **633 KiB**. That's the whole clone. It is not twenty minutes of anything.

The obvious-looking culprit was `assets/sample.bin` — a 3 MiB binary added in `d9456eb` and deleted in `925a138`, so it's dead history weight that every clone still carries. The standard fix is a `git filter-repo` purge and a force-push.

I checked its packed size before doing that:

```
b7f1f882…  blob  3145728  3075  631425
                 ↑raw     ↑in-pack
```

**3,075 bytes.** The file is highly compressible, so git already stores it in 3 KB. Purging it would have shaved 0.5% off a 633 KiB clone while rewriting every commit SHA, invalidating every existing clone, and requiring a coordinated force-push. I left history alone — there is nothing to win there. Same for the largest real object, `ParseBenchmarkData.zip` at 68 KB.

No submodules, no LFS, no hooks. Git is genuinely not the bottleneck.

## Where the twenty minutes actually goes

Maven filling an empty `~/.m2` on first build. The default `mvn verify` builds all seven modules, and four exist only to test Gson against external toolchains that must each be downloaded: GraalVM native-image (`test-graal-native-image`), ProGuard + R8 (`test-shrinker`), a `protoc` binary + protobuf + Guava (`proto`), and Caliper + `jackson-databind` (`metrics`). On a modern JDK, Spotless and Error Prone resolve too — their `disable-*` profiles auto-activate only on *older* JDKs, so nobody gets them skipped by default.

New joiners are timing clone-plus-first-build and calling it "the clone."

## What I changed

Rewrote the root `README.md` (it was three empty newlines) with the fast path:

```bash
mvn -pl gson -am test -P disable-spotless,disable-error-prone
```

plus when to reach for the full build, parallel/offline flags, and the `--filter=blob:none` clone option noted honestly as marginal here. Every module and profile name in it is verified against the poms. I also repacked the object store — 455 loose objects, zero packs — which is safe maintenance; `git fsck` is clean and all seven commits are intact.

The README is modified but uncommitted; I didn't commit since you didn't ask.

Two things worth your attention:

- **A live credential is in the history.** `f1d171a` added `config.secret`, `925a138` removed it, but `git show f1d171a:config.secret` still returns the token and anyone who has ever cloned has it. Rotate it — a history rewrite wouldn't un-leak it, so rotation is the actual fix, independent of anything above.
- **I didn't empirically time a cold Maven build** — no network here. The heavy modules are identified from the poms and corroborated by CI already excluding exactly `!metrics,!test-graal-native-image,!test-jpms,!test-shrinker` in its reproducible-build job. Worth having one new joiner time the fast path against the old one to confirm the size of the win.
